messages:
leah: Quick one from onboarding: Rust SDK sample app behaves oddly on fast reconnects. Sometimes a mid-stream fragment gets split and the parser emits a partial token as a separate event, which looks like out-of-order output.

omar: Can you paste a tiny repro?

leah: Minimal repro with our sample server and the rust client: run the sample, send a stream, then kill+restart client within ~150ms. Repro rate ~20% on my laptop. Rust SDK v0.3.2.

leah: curl repro (server side):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d '{"prompt":"rust reconnect test"}'
```

leah: Rust client logs show: "frame_parsed: chunk: \"hel\"" then "frame_parsed: chunk: \"lo\"" and sometimes "resume_token" lands between them, so UI flips.

kevin: Hmm. Rust BytesMut behavior + split_off could yield boundary splits if we assume full delimiter always present. Python/node parsers are more forgiving.

omar: Two fixes: 1) change parser to buffer until the full delimiter sequence is seen (don't treat \n as guaranteed chunk boundary), 2) server could add lightweight per-chunk seq numbers in the resume metadata to make reordering safe.

leah: I can PR a conservative parser change in the Rust SDK (hold partial tokens until delimiter). Also add a unit test that simulates mid-chunk abort + resume.

ci-bot: CI run 7882 attached: https://ci.redwood.ai/build/7882 (rust-stream-e2e flaky)

kevin: Add parity test across node/python/rust in the streaming e2e harness. Also file an internal issue so onboarding docs can note the workaround (200ms reconnect delay).

leah: Filed: https://redwood.internal/issue/RED-4755. Will include a sample flag to enable safe-reconnect mode in the rust sample app and link the dedupe helper snippet.

devx-bot: Note added to onboarding checklist: "If using Rust SDK, recommend 200ms reconnect backoff until server+SDK patch lands." :white_check_mark:

omar: Great. Prioritize the Rust parser fix + parity test. We should keep the server seq-id option as a follow-up if other SDKs also need it.
